tasks.name: Draft X thread: Compound domain incident × Anticapture Interface Hijack validation
tasks.description:
Draft a Twitter/X thread for Zeugh about today's Compound domain phishing incident (Mar 9 2026) and how it validates the Anticapture framework's Interface Hijack metric.

KEY ANGLE: This is NOT about rating Compound's governance stage. It's about showing the framework correctly identifies interface-layer attacks as a real, recurring, cheap governance capture vector.

FACTS TO USE (verified):
- compound.finance redirected to phishing domain compOOnd via infrastructure account compromise
- app.compound.finance (IPFS-served) was untouched — independently verified, zero fund losses
- 3rd interface-layer incident for Compound in 18 months (Jul 2024 frontend, Sep 2024 Discord, Mar 2026 DNS redirect)
- Anticapture framework metric 13 (Interface Hijack) specifically tracks whether DAO domains follow DNS protection standards
- IPFS content-hash verification is the proven protection — Compounds own app proves it works
- The attack costs orders of magnitude less than on-chain governance capture but can bypass every on-chain protection
- Framework built from studying 30+ real governance attacks — today adds another data point

TONE: Analytical, constructive. Credit Compound for IPFS architecture saving users. Frame as framework validation, not a dunk.

DO NOT fabricate quotes or attribute statements to anyone.

SOURCE: https://www.comp.xyz/t/security-update-by-compound-ssps-compound-finance-domain-redirect-incident/7675
